# Bash with prompt tools: the OSC 133 marks Tessera's injection gives, by
# spec task 158 (wave 24, 2026-11-17), section 5 table X and section 6 M1.
# Read by tests/bash_tools.rs. Fields are separated by ` | `; `-` is empty.
#
# Mark rows: id | route | startup files (tests/fixtures/bash-tools/, sourced
# in this order) | marks of the first prompt | marks of the first command |
# the same two on bash 5.1 and later, where PROMPT_COMMAND can be an array
# (bash-preexec 0.6 and later and the stand-in make one, oh-my-bash appends
# an element). An array is integrated with one element of ours, or with
# bash-preexec's hooks once bash-preexec is loaded (ADR 0021 amendment,
# #613). bash-preexec 0.6 makes the array at its first prompt, after the
# handshake and that prompt's OSC 7.
# The route is `login` (`bash -l`: the PROMPT_COMMAND loader, files sourced
# from .bash_profile) or `rcfile` (`bash -i`: `--rcfile`, from .bashrc);
# `login-alone` rows are login shells the scan leaves to bash (B5h:
# oh-my-bash's `PROMPT_COMMAND+=(...)`), not run.
# Every row also holds, for 20 prompts: no error output, one handshake
# before the first prompt, no D before the first A, no C but right after a
# B, and from the second prompt on `D;<status>` for the last command, then
# A B and C for the next one.
#
# X2/X3: starship rewrites PS1 after the loader ran (lead decision D3, 2026-11-17): the
# first prompt and the first command are unmarked.
# X5, X7, X14e on bash >= 5.1: oh-my-bash's array element runs after the loader,
# or after bash-preexec's install entry, in the array bash copied for that
# prompt, and rebuilds PS1: unmarked in the same way. (0.7.0 appends its entry
# after oh-my-bash's, X6, so there the install runs last; 0.6.0 and 0.5.0 put
# theirs into element 0.)
# X8g, X14f, X15e on bash >= 5.1 (bash-preexec, then oh-my-bash, --rcfile):
# oh-my-bash's element runs after bash-preexec's install in the array bash
# copied for the first prompt and rebuilds PS1: that prompt and its command
# are unmarked; marked from the second prompt on (#613, accepted deviation).
# X16a on bash >= 5.1 (login): measured fully marked, where the #613 spec
# predicted an unmarked first prompt (accepted deviation).
mark | X1 | login | - | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X2 | login | starship-init-1.27.bash | - | - | - | -
mark | X3 | login | starship-init-master.bash | - | - | - | -
mark | X4 | login | bash-preexec-install.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X5 | login-alone | oh-my-bash-prompt.sh | A B | C | - | -
mark | X6 | login-alone | oh-my-bash-prompt.sh bash-preexec-install.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X7 | login-alone | bash-preexec-install.sh oh-my-bash-prompt.sh | A B | C | - | -
mark | X8a | rcfile | - | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X8b | rcfile | starship-init-1.27.bash | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X8c | rcfile | starship-init-master.bash | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X8d | rcfile | bash-preexec-install.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X8e | rcfile | oh-my-bash-prompt.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X8f | rcfile | oh-my-bash-prompt.sh bash-preexec-install.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X8g | rcfile | bash-preexec-install.sh oh-my-bash-prompt.sh | A B | C | - | -
# bash-preexec with starship loaded after it (starship then uses its hook lists).
mark | X9a | login | bash-preexec-install.sh starship-init-1.27.bash | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X9b | rcfile | bash-preexec-install.sh starship-init-1.27.bash | A B | C | A B | C
# bash-preexec 0.5.0 and 0.6.0: another install text than 0.7.0.
mark | X14a | login | bash-preexec-0.6.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X14b | rcfile | bash-preexec-0.6.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X14c | login | bash-preexec-0.5.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X14d | rcfile | bash-preexec-0.5.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X14e | login-alone | oh-my-bash-prompt.sh bash-preexec-0.6.sh | A B | C | - | -
mark | X14f | rcfile | bash-preexec-0.6.sh oh-my-bash-prompt.sh | A B | C | - | -
# bash-preexec 0.7.0 on its DEBUG trap path (bash 5.1 and 5.2; 5.3 takes PS0).
mark | X15a | login | bash-preexec-debug.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X15b | rcfile | bash-preexec-debug.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X15c | login-alone | oh-my-bash-prompt.sh bash-preexec-debug.sh | A B | C | A B | C
mark | X15d | login-alone | bash-preexec-debug.sh oh-my-bash-prompt.sh | A B | C | - | -
mark | X15e | rcfile | bash-preexec-debug.sh oh-my-bash-prompt.sh | A B | C | - | -
# A theme's entry added after bash-preexec's install entry. Login on 3.2: both
# are in the text bash is running when the loader runs, so the theme rebuilds
# PS1 after the install. With an array the install is a later element.
mark | X16a | login | bash-preexec-install.sh appended-theme.sh | - | - | A B | C
mark | X16b | rcfile | bash-preexec-install.sh appended-theme.sh | A B | C | A B | C
#
# OSC 7 rows (M1): id | directory name (`\n` is a newline) | its encoding,
# Terminal.app's rule: every byte outside [/._~A-Za-z0-9-] is %XX.
osc7 | M1a | a b | a%20b
osc7 | M1b | é | %C3%A9
osc7 | M1c | 100% | 100%25
osc7 | M1d | nl\nx | nl%0Ax
osc7 | M1e | ~x.y_z-1 | ~x.y_z-1
osc7 | M1f | Plain09 | Plain09

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wave 27 rows (#158 and #540), from the spec-researcher's table of
# 2026-11-22 (scratch/spec-researcher-158/bash_spec_wave27.txt; sources: the
# GNU bash manual sections named per row, kitty.bash, ghostty.bash, and
# measurements on /bin/bash 3.2.57 and Homebrew bash 5.3). Read by
# tests/bash_rows.rs, one test per row. In these rows a command field holds
# one line per Enter, separated by `\n`; `\|` is a pipe (` | ` separates
# fields). `base`: the injected shell prints what the same bash prints
# without the injection (every line that is not a prompt, errors included).
# `base after N`: the same, past the first N such lines (the loading prompt,
# B6b). `limit: a / b`: an ACCEPTED LIMIT (ADR 0021): the injected shell
# prints exactly the lines a, b, which differ from base. `lines: a / b`:
# the injected shell prints exactly a, b (B5: the user's entry runs at every
# prompt; without the injection some of these appends are a syntax error).
# `base ignoring W`: base once every line `W` is dropped, with at least as
# many `W` lines as base (P17: the user's DEBUG trap also runs for the
# hooks' first commands at each prompt, as on main; ACCEPTED LIMIT). The
# pipestatus rows run on the rcfile and the login route, the pc rows (the
# loader's) on the login route.
#
# PIPESTATUS (#540):
# pipestatus | id | bashes | commands | expected
pipestatus | P1 | 3.2 5.3 | true \| false \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]} rc=$?" | base
pipestatus | P2 | 3.2 5.3 | false \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]} rc=$?" | base
pipestatus | P3 | 3.2 5.3 | true \| true \| false \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]} rc=$?" | base
pipestatus | P4 | 3.2 5.3 | true \| false\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]} rc=$?" | base
pipestatus | P5 | 3.2 5.3 | false\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]} rc=$?" | base
pipestatus | P6 | 3.2 5.3 | echo a b LASTARG\necho "us=[$_]" | base
pipestatus | P7 | 3.2 5.3 | echo a b LASTARG\ntrue \| false\necho "us=[$_] ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}" | base
pipestatus | P8 | 3.2 5.3 | set -o pipefail\nfalse \| true \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]} rc=$?" | base
pipestatus | P9 | 3.2 5.3 | ! false \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]} rc=$?" | base
pipestatus | P10 | 3.2 5.3 | true \| false \| true; echo "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}" | base
pipestatus | P11 | 3.2 5.3 | IFS=,\ntrue \| false \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}" | base
pipestatus | P12 | 3.2 5.3 | trap 'echo ERRTRAP' ERR\ntrue \| false \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"\ntrue \| true \| false\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}" | base
pipestatus | P13 | 3.2 5.3 | set -e\ntrue \| false \| false \|\| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"\ntrue \| false \| false\necho alive | base
pipestatus | P14 | 3.2 | shopt -s extdebug\ntrue \| false \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]} rc=$?" | limit: ps=0 rc=0
pipestatus | P15 | 3.2 | true \| true \| true \| true \| true \| true \| true \| true \| true \| false \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}" | limit: ps=0
pipestatus | P15b | 3.2 5.3 | true \| true \| true \| true \| true \| true \| true \| false \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}" | base
pipestatus | P16 | 3.2 5.3 | true \| false \| true\n\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}" | base
pipestatus | P17 | 3.2 5.3 | trap 'echo DBG' DEBUG\ntrue \| false \| true\necho "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}" | base ignoring DBG
# The gate: only a command line naming PIPESTATUS gets it back on 3.2; a
# function reading it at its start sees the hooks' one status.
pipestatus | G1 | 3.2 | f() { echo "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; }\ntrue \| false \| true\nf | limit: ps=0
pipestatus | G1b | 5.3 | f() { echo "ps=${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; }\ntrue \| false \| true\nf | base
# P18 (bash 4+ keeps PIPESTATUS around the trap itself: no restore, no
# fork) is tests/bash_rows.rs `p18_bash_4_restores_nothing`.
#
# Appends to PROMPT_COMMAND in .bash_profile, on the login route (B5, B6):
# pc | id | bashes | .bash_profile | commands | expected
pc | B5a | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND+='echo USER_PC' | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
pc | B5b | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND+='echo USER_PC;' | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
pc | B5c | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND="${PROMPT_COMMAND}echo USER_PC;" | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
pc | B5d | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND="$PROMPT_COMMAND echo USER_PC" | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
pc | B5e | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND+=$'\\necho USER_PC' | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
pc | B5f | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND="${PROMPT_COMMAND:+$PROMPT_COMMAND;}echo USER_PC" | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
pc | B5g | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND="$PROMPT_COMMAND; echo USER_PC" | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
pc | B5h | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND+=("echo USER_PC") | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
pc | B5i | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='history -a; echo USER_PC' | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
# The scan's own choices (ADR 0021): blanks before a separator still lead
# with the separator; a `$x` the scan cannot read counts as glued; `&&`
# leads like `;`.
pc | B5j | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND="$PROMPT_COMMAND ; echo USER_PC" | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
pc | B5k | 3.2 5.3 | x=echo; PROMPT_COMMAND="$PROMPT_COMMAND$x USER_PC" | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
pc | B5l | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND="$PROMPT_COMMAND && echo USER_PC" | true\ntrue | lines: USER_PC / USER_PC / USER_PC
# Both kinds of append: no terminator serves both, bash is left alone.
pc | B5m | 3.2 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND+='echo A1'\nPROMPT_COMMAND="$PROMPT_COMMAND; echo A2" | true\ntrue | lines: A1 / A2 / A1 / A2 / A1 / A2
pc | B6a | 3.2 5.3 | rc() { return $1; }; __ps() { local e=$? p="${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; echo "PSEEN e=$e ps=$p"; }; PROMPT_COMMAND="${PROMPT_COMMAND:+$PROMPT_COMMAND;}__ps" | rc 7\ntrue\nrc 3\ntrue \| false \| true\ntrue | base after 1
pc | B6c | 3.2 5.3 | rc() { return $1; }; __ps() { local e=$? p="${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; echo "PSEEN e=$e ps=$p"; }; PROMPT_COMMAND+=$'\\n__ps' | rc 7\ntrue\nrc 3\ntrue \| false \| true\ntrue | base after 1
pc | B6e | 3.2 5.3 | rc() { return $1; }; __ps() { local e=$? p="${PIPESTATUS[*]}"; echo "PSEEN e=$e ps=$p"; }; PROMPT_COMMAND+=';__ps' | rc 7\ntrue\nrc 3\ntrue \| false \| true\ntrue | lines: PSEEN e=0 ps=0 / PSEEN e=7 ps=7 / PSEEN e=0 ps=0 / PSEEN e=3 ps=3 / PSEEN e=0 ps=0 1 0 / PSEEN e=0 ps=0

# M10: launches whose `--rcfile` bash 3.2 or 5.x does not read take the
# loader, so no TESSERA_ variable is in the shell (tests/bash_rows.rs runs
# `env` in each, on both bashes).
# rcfile | id | environment (`-`: none) | arguments
rcfile | R1 | - | --norc
rcfile | R2 | - | -norc
rcfile | R3 | - | --posix
rcfile | R4 | - | -posix
rcfile | R5 | - | -o posix
rcfile | R6 | - | -o posix -i
rcfile | R7 | POSIXLY_CORRECT=1 | -i
rcfile | R8 | POSIXLY_CORRECT=1 | --noprofile
rcfile | R9 | POSIXLY_CORRECT=1 | -norc
rcfile | R10 | POSIXLY_CORRECT=1 | -l
rcfile | R11 | SHELLOPTS=braceexpand:posix | -i
#
# The --rcfile route's end of the startup file (#659): a `.bashrc` that
# runs `set -e` and ends in a failing `&&` list or in `return N` keeps the
# shell, as without Tessera (the status `source` returns for it no longer
# trips `set -e`), while `set -e` still stops the file, and the shell, at
# a failing command inside it. The first prompt's PROMPT_COMMAND entry
# (`pc=`) and the first command (`st=`) see bash's own status of the file
# (`return N` leaves the status before it). The `.bashrc` is the field
# exactly (one line per `\n`; the prompt comes from the environment), so
# it ends with the field's last line. On the --rcfile route only.
# `lines: a / b`: the injected shell prints exactly a, b, and so does the
# same bash without the injection; `lines: -`: neither prints anything
# (both exit before their first prompt). E1 also checks that neither our
# RETURN trap nor a `_tessera_si_rc_` variable is left after startup.
# E10 is an ACCEPTED LIMIT: the
# startup file's own RETURN trap replaces ours (`limit:` as above).
# rcexit | id | bashes | .bashrc | commands | expected
rcexit | E1 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\nfalse && true | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}"\necho "rt=[$(trap -p RETURN)] v=[$(compgen -v _tessera_si_rc_)]" | lines: pc=1 / st=1 e=e / pc=0 / rt=[] v=[] / pc=0
rcexit | E2 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\nfalse\necho after | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: -
rcexit | E3 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\nf() { false; echo in-f; }\nf\necho after | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: -
rcexit | E4 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\ntrue\nreturn 3 | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: pc=0 / st=0 e=e / pc=0
rcexit | E5 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\nfalse && true\nreturn 3 | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: pc=1 / st=1 e=e / pc=0
rcexit | E6 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nfalse && true | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: pc=1 / st=1 e= / pc=0
rcexit | E7 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nfalse | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: pc=1 / st=1 e= / pc=0
rcexit | E8 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nfalse\nreturn 3 | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: pc=1 / st=1 e= / pc=0
rcexit | E9 | 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND=('echo "pc=$?"')\nset -e\nfalse && true | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: pc=1 / st=1 e=e / pc=0
rcexit | E10 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\ntrap 'echo R' RETURN\nfalse && true | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | limit: R
rcexit | E11 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\n. /dev/null\nset -T\ng() { :; }\ng\nfalse && true | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: pc=1 / st=1 e=e / pc=0
# A syntax error ends the file with source's status, bash's own on 5.x;
# on 3.2 bash alone has 258 (ACCEPTED LIMIT, as before #659). Standard
# error, where bash reports it with the file's path, goes to /dev/null
# until the first prompt's entry puts it back.
rcexit | E12 | 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='s=$?; exec 2>&1; echo "pc=$s"'\nexec 2>/dev/null\nfi | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: pc=2 / st=2 e= / pc=0
rcexit | E13 | 3.2 | PROMPT_COMMAND='s=$?; exec 2>&1; echo "pc=$s"'\nexec 2>/dev/null\nfi | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | limit: pc=1 / st=1 e= / pc=0
# `set -E` under `shopt -s nocasematch` is not `set -e` (#659 B1): the
# trap tests the option, not `$-`.
rcexit | E14 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nshopt -s nocasematch\nset -E | false\necho alive | lines: pc=0 / pc=1 / alive / pc=0
# A `.bashrc` that sources tessera.bash itself (#676), with its own
# TESSERA_SHELL_INTEGRATION (that load is the live one) or without (the
# injected words load it after the file): the source is harmless under
# `set -e`, the file's end keeps its status, and nothing of the --rcfile
# route's end is left. The script is the one the run materialised.
rcexit | E15 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\nTESSERA_SHELL_INTEGRATION=enabled . "$HOME"/../scripts/*/bash/tessera.bash\necho sourced | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}"\necho "rt=[$(trap -p RETURN)] v=[$(compgen -v _tessera_si_rc_)] f=[$(compgen -A function _tessera_si_rc_)]" | lines: sourced / pc=0 / st=0 e=e / pc=0 / rt=[] v=[] f=[] / pc=0
rcexit | E16 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\n. "$HOME"/../scripts/*/bash/tessera.bash\nfalse && true | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}"\necho "rt=[$(trap -p RETURN)] v=[$(compgen -v _tessera_si_rc_)] f=[$(compgen -A function _tessera_si_rc_)]" | lines: pc=1 / st=1 e=e / pc=0 / rt=[] v=[] f=[] / pc=0
rcexit | E17 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\nTESSERA_SHELL_INTEGRATION=enabled . "$HOME"/../scripts/*/bash/tessera.bash\nfalse && true | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: pc=1 / st=1 e=e / pc=0
rcexit | E18 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -e\nTESSERA_SHELL_INTEGRATION=enabled . "$HOME"/../scripts/*/bash/tessera.bash | echo "st=$? e=${-//[^e]/}" | lines: pc=0 / st=0 e=e / pc=0
# A Ctrl-C while the `.bashrc` runs (#713): bash alone drops the rest of
# its startup; the injected shell returns from the file instead, so the
# rest of tessera.bash runs: neither our RETURN or INT trap nor a
# `_tessera_si_rc` variable or function is left (E19), and the first
# prompt sees 130 (E20). `^C <text>` in the commands is a Ctrl-C once the
# shell printed the text, which comes from where the Ctrl-C is to land.
# No row kills a child: bash 3.2 gives it the terminal late, and a Ctrl-C
# before that reaches only the shell (bash alone then waits for the
# child). ACCEPTED LIMITS: inside a function the file called, the Ctrl-C
# returns from that function and the file goes on, where bash alone drops
# the rest (E21); after a loop bash 3.2 alone shows 128, not 130 (E22).
rcexit | E19 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | echo READY\nwhile (( SECONDS < 20 )); do :; done\necho after | ^C READY\necho "rt=[$(trap -p RETURN)] it=[$(trap -p INT)] v=[$(compgen -v _tessera_si_rc)] f=[$(compgen -A function _tessera_si_rc)]" | lines: READY / rt=[] it=[] v=[] f=[]
rcexit | E20 | 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\necho READY\nwhile (( SECONDS < 20 )); do :; done\necho after | ^C READY\necho "st=$?" | lines: READY / pc=130 / st=130 / pc=0
rcexit | E21 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | f() { echo READY; while (( SECONDS < 20 )); do :; done; }\nf\necho after-f | ^C READY | limit: READY / after-f
rcexit | E22 | 3.2 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\necho READY\nwhile (( SECONDS < 20 )); do :; done\necho after | ^C READY\necho "st=$?" | limit: READY / pc=130 / st=130 / pc=0
# A Ctrl-C after the file returned, while the rest of tessera.bash runs
# (E23): bash 3.2 runs startup files as a non-interactive shell, where
# `trap - INT` makes SIGINT end the shell until its interactive handler
# is back after the startup files, so our INT trap stays (a no-op once the
# file returned) until the route's last command. The file's DEBUG trap
# holds the rest of the script at a command run after the file returned
# (bash alone: at the file's last command).
rcexit | E23 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | trap 'if [[ $BASH_COMMAND == "builtin unset _tessera_si_rc_depth"* || ( $BASH_COMMAND == : && -z ${_tessera_si_rc_depth+x} ) ]]; then trap - DEBUG; echo READY; s=$SECONDS; while (( SECONDS - s < 4 )); do :; done; fi' DEBUG\n: | ^C READY\necho "it=[$(trap -p INT)]" | lines: READY / it=[]
# A Ctrl-C in a DEBUG trap of the file's that runs after our INT trap is
# gone (E24, E25): none does, the route's end is our last command and
# runs with `set -T` off (put back inside it). The trap holds at the
# first command it sees with no INT trap after the file returned: here
# and with bash alone, the first prompt's PROMPT_COMMAND. E24 ends with
# status 0 (no command after the end), E25 with 1 under `set -T`.
rcexit | E24 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND=:\ntrap 'if [[ -z ${_tessera_si_rc_depth+x} && -z $(trap -p INT) ]]; then trap - DEBUG; echo READY; s=$SECONDS; while (( SECONDS - s < 4 )); do :; done; fi' DEBUG | ^C READY\necho "it=[$(trap -p INT)]" | lines: READY / it=[]
rcexit | E25 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND=:\nset -T\ntrap 'if [[ -z ${_tessera_si_rc_depth+x} && -z $(trap -p INT) ]]; then trap - DEBUG; echo READY; s=$SECONDS; while (( SECONDS - s < 4 )); do :; done; fi' DEBUG\nfalse | ^C READY\necho "it=[$(trap -p INT)] t=${-//[^T]/}" | lines: READY / it=[] t=T
# A DEBUG trap of the file's under `set -T` or `shopt -s extdebug` runs in
# the route's command substitutions too (#726): one that writes to standard
# output (E26, E27) or to descriptor 3 (E28, E29), or, under extdebug, one
# whose non-zero status skips the next command there (E30). The check that
# our INT trap is still the one in place runs with `set -T` off, so the
# trap is removed after the file, and the startup status, `set -T` and
# extdebug come out as bash alone leaves them. (Measured before the fix:
# E26 left the trap on 3.2 and 5.3, E27 on 5.3; with a read through
# descriptor 3, E28 on 3.2 and 5.3, E29 and E30 on 5.3.)
rcexit | E26 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nset -T\ntrap '[[ $BASH_SUBSHELL == 0 ]] || echo sub' DEBUG\nfalse | echo "it=[$(trap -p INT)] t=${-//[^T]/}" | lines: pc=1 / it=[sub] t=T / pc=0
rcexit | E27 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nshopt -s extdebug\ntrap '[[ $BASH_SUBSHELL == 0 ]] || echo sub' DEBUG\nfalse | shopt -q extdebug; x=$?; echo "it=[$(trap -p INT)] t=${-//[^T]/} x=$x" | lines: pc=1 / it=[sub] t=T x=0 / pc=0
rcexit | E28 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nexec 3>/dev/null\nset -T\ntrap '[[ $BASH_SUBSHELL == 0 ]] || echo sub >&3' DEBUG\nfalse | echo "it=[$(trap -p INT)] t=${-//[^T]/}" | lines: pc=1 / it=[] t=T / pc=0
rcexit | E29 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nexec 3>/dev/null\nshopt -s extdebug\ntrap '[[ $BASH_SUBSHELL == 0 ]] || echo sub >&3' DEBUG\nfalse | shopt -q extdebug; x=$?; echo "it=[$(trap -p INT)] t=${-//[^T]/} x=$x" | lines: pc=1 / it=[] t=T x=0 / pc=0
rcexit | E30 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='echo "pc=$?"'\nshopt -s extdebug\ntrap '[[ $BASH_SUBSHELL == 0 ]]' DEBUG\nfalse | shopt -q extdebug; x=$?; trap -p INT > it; read -r l < it; echo "it=[$l] t=${-//[^T]/} x=$x" | lines: pc=1 / it=[] t=T x=0 / pc=0
# Under `set -x` with BASH_XTRACEFD=1 (bash 4.1 and later; 3.2 always
# traces to standard error) the trace of the route's `trap -p INT` went
# into the read (#733), so our INT trap stayed: E31, and E33 with `set -T`
# and a DEBUG trap as in E26. E32 (the trace on standard error) and E34 (on
# descriptor 5, a file) passed before the fix too: they, like E31 and E33,
# check that `set -x` is back on after the check ($- as bash alone leaves
# it, but for `s`, which 5.x adds) and that no `_tessera_si_rc_` variable
# is left. The trace goes to /dev/null until the first PROMPT_COMMAND
# entry has saved $- and turned `set -x` off. (Measured before the fix:
# E31 and E33 left the trap on 5.3.) E35 traces to a file under `set -T`
# with a DEBUG trap: from the route's status after the file to the check's
# end, the trace has no `set -T`, `set +T` or `trap -p` line (`set -x` goes
# off before `set -T` and comes back after it).
rcexit | E31 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='s=$? f=$-; set +x; exec 2>&7 >&6; echo "pc=$s f=${f//s/}"'\nexec 6>&1 7>&2 >/dev/null 2>/dev/null\nBASH_XTRACEFD=1\nset -x\nfalse | echo "it=[$(trap -p INT)] v=[$(compgen -v _tessera_si_rc_)]" | lines: pc=1 f=himxBH / it=[] v=[] / pc=0 f=himBH
rcexit | E32 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='s=$? f=$-; set +x; exec 2>&7 >&6; echo "pc=$s f=${f//s/}"'\nexec 6>&1 7>&2 >/dev/null 2>/dev/null\nset -x\nfalse | echo "it=[$(trap -p INT)] v=[$(compgen -v _tessera_si_rc_)]" | lines: pc=1 f=himxBH / it=[] v=[] / pc=0 f=himBH
rcexit | E33 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='s=$? f=$-; set +x; exec 2>&7 >&6; echo "pc=$s f=${f//s/}"'\nexec 6>&1 7>&2 >/dev/null 2>/dev/null\nBASH_XTRACEFD=1\nset -T\ntrap '[[ $BASH_SUBSHELL == 0 ]] || echo sub' DEBUG\nset -x\nfalse | echo "it=[$(trap -p INT)] f=${-//s/} v=[$(compgen -v _tessera_si_rc_)]" | lines: pc=1 f=himxBHT / it=[sub] f=himBHT v=[sub] / pc=0 f=himBHT
rcexit | E34 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='s=$? f=$-; set +x; exec 2>&7 >&6; echo "pc=$s f=${f//s/}"'\nexec 6>&1 7>&2 >/dev/null 2>/dev/null 5>xt\nBASH_XTRACEFD=5\nset -x\nfalse | echo "it=[$(trap -p INT)] v=[$(compgen -v _tessera_si_rc_)]" | lines: pc=1 f=himxBH / it=[] v=[] / pc=0 f=himBH
rcexit | E35 | 3.2 5.1 5.3 | PROMPT_COMMAND='s=$? f=$-; set +x; exec 2>&7 >&6; echo "pc=$s f=${f//s/}"'\nexec 6>&1 7>&2 >/dev/null 2>/dev/null 5>xt\nBASH_XTRACEFD=5\nset -T\ntrap ': dbg' DEBUG\nset -x\nfalse | awk '/_tessera_si_rc_status=/ { a = 1 } a && /-lt 256/ { exit } a' xt > ck; echo "n=$(grep -cE 'set [-+]T|trap -p' ck) it=[$(trap -p INT)] v=[$(compgen -v _tessera_si_rc_)]" | lines: pc=1 f=himxBHT / n=0 it=[] v=[] / pc=0 f=himBHT
